best_architecture: Use the high-level McpServer class (from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js) rather than the low-level Server + setRequestHandler API. McpServer wraps the protocol layer and handles capability negotiation, request routing, and automatic Zod-to-JSON-Schema conversion + runtime input validation. The recommended pattern is a modular, domain-driven, layered architecture that separates three concerns: (1) protocol/transport wiring, (2) tool business logic, and (3) shared services/state. Concretely, structure the project as src/index.ts (entry point + server bootstrap + transport selection + graceful shutdown), src/tools/ (one file per domain, each exporting a registration function), src/schemas/ (Zod schemas, one per tool), src/services/ (shared API clients, IPC to the Python orchestrator, retry/timeout logic), src/types.ts (z.infer-derived types), and src/constants.ts. For 20+ tools, the critical decision is to NOT register every tool inline in index.ts: instead give each tool module a registerXxxTools(server) function and call them from a central registry, OR adopt directory-based auto-discovery (as mcp-framework does). Each tool is registered via server.registerTool(name, {title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations}, handler). Key design decisions that matter most: (1) STDIO HYGIENE -- stdout is reserved exclusively for JSON-RPC messages; ALL logging MUST go to stderr (console.error or a stderr-bound logger). A single stray console.log to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC stream and breaks the client. This is the #1 architectural constraint for a stdio server. (2) NEVER throw from a tool handler -- catch all errors and return a CallToolResult with isError:true and a text content block; an uncaught throw can crash the server or produce a protocol-level error rather than a tool-level error the LLM can recover from. (3) Use Zod with .strict() and .describe() on every field so unknown keys are rejected and the LLM gets rich JSON Schema descriptions. (4) Provide structuredContent (machine-readable) alongside content[].text (human/LLM-readable) when an outputSchema is declared. (5) For large outputs, enforce a CHARACTER_LIMIT (~25k chars) and truncate with a helpful message + pagination (offset/limit, has_more, next_offset) so a single tool call cannot blow the context window. (6) Graceful shutdown: register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that call transport.close()/server.close() and flush state before process.exit. (7) Tool naming: snake_case, service/domain-prefixed (e.g. fs_read_file, git_commit) to avoid collisions across 20+ tools. Streaming over stdio: the stdio transport itself does not stream partial tool results within a single tool call (a CallToolResult is returned whole); for incremental progress use the MCP progress-notification mechanism (notifications/progress via a progressToken) and/or log to stderr -- true chunked streaming is a feature of the Streamable HTTP transport, not stdio. For Local-Claw (Python orchestrator <-> TS server over stdin/stdout) stdio is the correct transport: it is the simplest, most secure (no network surface, OS process isolation), and lowest-latency option. Enable TypeScript strict mode, target ES2022, use ESM ("type": "module", module/moduleResolution Node16+), and prefer unknown over any.
reference_papers: Model Context Protocol Specification (Anthropic, 2024-2025) - the canonical normative reference (JSON-RPC 2.0 client-server, lifecycle/initialization handshake, capability negotiation, tools/resources/prompts). Spec version 2025-11-25 at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25 -- not an arXiv paper but the authoritative source [uncertain: spec is versioned and evolving]

A Survey of Agent Interoperability Protocols: Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent Communication Protocol (ACP), Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A), and Agent Network Protocol (ANP) (Ehtesham et al. 2025) - arxiv:2505.02279

ScaleMCP: Dynamic and Auto-Synchronizing Model Context Protocol Tools for LLM Agents (2025) - arxiv:2505.06416 - relevant for dynamic registration / auto-sync of large tool sets (the 20+ tool scaling concern)
Unified Tool Integration for LLMs: A Protocol-Agnostic Approach to Function Calling (2025) - arxiv:2508.02979
Enhancing Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Context-Aware Server Collaboration (2026) - arxiv:2601.11595 [uncertain: very recent, verify final venue/ID]

Note: MCP is an engineering standard, not an academic field; the most load-bearing references are the official spec + SDK docs rather than papers. The protocol's message-passing design is explicitly modeled on the Language Server Protocol (LSP).
reference_repos: modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk - the official TypeScript SDK (McpServer, Server, StdioServerTransport, StreamableHTTPServerTransport); see docs/server.md for the canonical tool registration patterns - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk

anthropics/skills (skills/mcp-builder/reference/node_mcp_server.md) - Anthropic's own production reference guide for Node/TS MCP servers: project structure, registerTool pattern, Zod .strict() schemas, error handling, truncation, pagination, dual transport - https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/mcp-builder/reference/node_mcp_server.md

cyanheads/mcp-ts-template - best production-grade template: modular domain-driven architecture, declarative tools/resources, pluggable auth, multi-backend storage, OpenTelemetry observability, stdio + HTTP transports - https://github.com/cyanheads/mcp-ts-template

yigitkonur/example-mcp-server-stdio - definitive educational STDIO reference: layered architecture, fail-fast error handling, and the critical stdout(JSON-RPC)-vs-stderr(logging) distinction - https://github.com/yigitkonur/example-mcp-server-stdio

cyanheads/git-mcp-server - real-world 'many tools' example: 28 Git tools across 7 categories, both stdio and Streamable HTTP - the best model for Local-Claw's 20+ tool registry - https://github.com/cyanheads/git-mcp-server

QuantGeekDev/mcp-framework - batteries-included TS framework with automatic directory-based discovery of tools/resources/prompts; useful pattern if Local-Claw wants auto-registration instead of manual wiring - https://github.com/QuantGeekDev/mcp-framework

aashari/boilerplate-mcp-server - layered boilerplate (CLI/tools/resources/controllers/services/utils), Zod v4 validation, dual transport with fallback, TOON output format for token reduction - https://github.com/aashari/boilerplate-mcp-server
johnleider/mcp - clean minimal modular example (tools/resources/prompts modules, stdio, dotenv) good for a from-scratch starting point - https://github.com/johnleider/mcp
key_libraries: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk - TypeScript/Node - latest 1.x (e.g. ~1.25.x; pin exact version, spec/SDK move fast) - core SDK providing McpServer, Server, StdioServerTransport, StreamableHTTPServerTransport, and types (CallToolResult, etc.); ~5.6M weekly npm downloads [uncertain: exact current version, was 1.6.1 in Anthropic's guide and 1.25.1 in later security analysis]

zod - TypeScript - v4 (or v3.25+ for back-compat) - runtime input/output validation; SDK imports zod/v4 internally and converts schemas to JSON Schema for the wire protocol; use .strict() and .describe(). Note: tool/prompt schemas now accept any Standard Schema library, so Valibot or ArkType are drop-in alternatives
typescript - v5.7+ - strict mode, ESM (module/moduleResolution Node16+), target ES2022; gives compile-time safety paired with Zod's runtime safety
tsx - dev dependency v4.19+ - run/watch TS directly during development without a separate build step
@types/node - dev dependency v22+ - Node type definitions
zod-to-json-schema - (transitive, used internally by the SDK) - converts Zod schemas to the JSON Schema the MCP protocol sends to clients; supports z.union/z.intersection via ZodType<object>
pino - TypeScript - optional structured logger configured to write to stderr (NEVER stdout) for a stdio server; alternative to console.error [uncertain: optional choice, not mandated]
valibot or arktype - TypeScript - optional alternative Standard Schema validators if a lighter-weight schema lib than Zod is desired [uncertain: optional]
uncertain: Exact current @modelcontextprotocol/sdk version (Anthropic guide cited ^1.6.1; later security analysis referenced 1.25.1 -- pin and verify on npm before use)
